decontamination_notes: Real bug fix from networkx/networkx PR #8837, merged 2026-08-21 — after the training cutoff of every model this suite targets; re-check upstream_merged against any newer model's cutoff before reusing. The Esfahanian algorithm-11 implementations of node_connectivity (connectivity.py) and minimum_node_cut (cuts.py) were derived for digraphs informally and carry five related bugs: the starting node is chosen by total degree instead of min(in-degree, out-degree); only one order of each ordered pair is checked although local node connectivity of a digraph pair is not symmetric; minimum_st_node_cut treats a t->s edge as making the pair inseparable although it is not an s-t path; self-loops inflate the degree bound and can put a node into its own cutset; and parallel edges inflate the bound on multigraphs. Symptoms are stark: minimum_node_cut on the directed triangle returns set() (not a cut at all), node_connectivity reports 1 for a digraph that is not strongly connected, and K5 with self-loops reports 6. Repo sliced at the PR base commit (7c635c9e) to the full networkx package plus LICENSE.txt (same slicing as the prior networkx tasks); networkx has no required runtime deps, so the base sandbox image runs the hidden tests with pytest and PYTHONPATH=. Coverage: 7 fail_to_pass tests, each verified failing at base and passing after the gold patch, spanning all five defects via public APIs (minimum_node_cut validity on the directed triangle, reverse-edge st-cut, weakly-connected zero connectivity, both-orders on weak and on strongly connected digraphs, self-loops, parallel edges); 5 pass_to_pass guards pin undirected results (K5, Petersen, path st-cuts, disconnected) and the already-correct directed cycle. Assertions check values and cut validity, never message text. Test constants come from the upstream PR's own test cases (graph shapes and expected numbers), generated from the gold patch behavior.
